log.msg: READ framework.css: .card = .surface plus padding: var(--pad-card), border-inline-start: 3px solid var(--card-edge, transparent), and :where(.card) > * + * { margin-block-start: var(--gap) }. The token and the class are well reasoned and not broken -- but the class bundles THREE things (surface colors, a reserved accent edge, and a child-rhythm rule) that only compose cleanly on a freestanding box with no rhythm of its own.

MEASURED BEFORE (headless, geometric padding -- child rect minus card rect, since a % inside calc() reads back from getComputedStyle as the calc string, never px): .dev-says-card (says.js, the mastermind log the owner complained about) -- padTop 12.8px at both 400px viewport (card 376.97px wide, mobile bottom sheet) and 1920px viewport (card 247.97px wide, desktop rail). Class list confirmed 'dev-says-card dev-says-card-mastermind dev-says-needs-you', padding: var(--pad) -- the page-region token, not --pad-card -- exactly what the padding-audit verifier already found.

DECISION: fixed the padding TOKEN only (padding: var(--pad) -> var(--pad-card)) on .dev-says-card, .dev-chat-card and .dev-chat-minion in devbar.css. Did NOT add the .card CLASS NAME to any of them. Reason, checked by reading .card's own rule: its child-rhythm line (:where(.card) > * + * { margin-block-start: var(--gap) }, ~15-24px) would ADD ON TOP of these cards' own flex `gap` (0.2em / 0.6em / 0.15em) rather than replace it -- a flex gap and a margin never cancel, so wearing the class in full would double the internal spacing between a card's meta row and its body. A card that already manages its own internal rhythm via flex gap takes the TOKEN directly; only a freestanding box with no rhythm of its own should take the whole class. This is a real, provable gap in the standard's own doc comment, which does not mention the flex-gap case -- worth a line in framework.css or the css skill for the next agent who reaches for .card on a compact list row.

SECOND REASON not to wear the full .card class here: .dev-bar's own background is var(--surface) (devbar.css line 24) -- the SAME token .card's own background declares. A card that fully adopted .card's background/border/radius would render the exact same fill as the rail it sits in, becoming invisible except for its 1px border. .dev-says-card and .dev-chat-card deliberately use var(--wash) (a visibly different, sunken tone) instead -- correct, and worth keeping. The standard as written only composes against a page whose ground is NOT already --surface; nested-in-a-surface is an unhandled case.

MEASURED AFTER, same method: .dev-says-card padTop is now 9.8px at 400px viewport (376.97px-wide card) and 6.44px at 1920px viewport (247.97px-wide card). Both match --pad-card's own formula, calc(clamp(0.5em, 2.6%, 2em) * var(--size)), computed at the dev bar's own 0.8rem (12.8px) font-size: 2.6% of 376.97px = 9.80px (between the 6.4px floor and the ceiling, so this is the number that lands); 2.6% of 247.97px = 6.45px, which is at the 6.4px floor. The token's value and the measured padding agree, to two decimal places. .dev-chat-minion (sessions tab) measured 9.73px uniform padding at 400px width after the same fix, visibly even, screenshot attached.

HONEST CAVEAT on the AFTER number: --pad-card correctly gives the dev bar LESS padding now (6.44-9.8px) than the previous var(--pad) floor did (12.8px) -- the fix is not free of tradeoffs. --pad-card's 0.5em floor was chosen and looked at against boxes wider than this rail (padding-audit tested 250/480/740/1400px cards, likely at a 1rem/16px font context, not this rail's 0.8rem/12.8px context, which is why my 6.44px floor differs from their measured ~8px at a similar 250px width). This is the token doing exactly what it says on narrow, small-type real estate -- not a bug -- but it is tighter than the 12.8px the owner had already seen and had not complained about again, and is close to the original ~5px complaint's neighborhood. Flagging as a WATCH, not a stop: if the owner finds the dev bar cards read as cramped again, --pad-card's 0.5em floor is the first number to revisit, not the dev bar's own CSS.

FOUND, NOT FIXED (out of this task's fence and scope -- a distinct bug, not caused by this padding change): at viewport widths under 34em the dev bar becomes a bottom sheet (devbar.css's own media query) and .dev-says-section (the mastermind log's own flex child inside .dev-body) computes to EXACTLY 0px height -- confirmed via getBoundingClientRect on a live page at 400px width: sectRect height 0, listRect height 0, while cardCount stayed 207 (the DOM is there, just invisible). Root cause read directly: .dev-body is a flex column of sections; the DEV SERVER / X-RAY / STRUCTURE / GO sections have no min-height override so the browser refuses to shrink them below their own text's content-size, while .dev-says-section explicitly sets min-height: 0 (needed for its own internal scrolling) -- under the bottom sheet's tight ~253px of body height, that makes the log section the ONLY one allowed to shrink, and it shrinks all the way to zero. This means the exact thing the owner complained about (the log) is currently invisible on a phone-width dev bar, a separate and arguably more serious bug than the padding one. Screenshot: shots/says-400-collapsed.png. Next fix: give the other four sections a shared max-height or move them behind a details/summary on narrow widths so the log keeps a real minimum height too.

CENSUS: grepped every CSS file under public/ for a selector whose class name contains 'card' or 'tile'. 196 distinct class names (207 file+name pairs, 366 total rule occurrences) -- independently close to the padding-audit's own count of 180 hand-rolled card/tile classes site-wide. Only 2 of those already reference --pad-card. Sampled a handful by hand (public/websites/Site.css .site-card, public/layouts/shell/shell.css .std-shell-card, public/resume/resume.css .resume-card, public/framework/ux/Popover/Popover.css .ux-popover-hostile-card) -- each is a genuine bordered/surfaced box holding a title and text, each with its own hand padding value, none wearing .card or --pad-card. public/framework/ai/v/3/** (out of bounds -- another minion owns it tonight) has its own v3.css card classes in the same shape and is exactly the kind of case that should adopt the standard next, once that rebuild lands.

NOT ADOPTED THIS PASS, named for the next one (verified to exist, not verified with a shot -- time budget): public/websites/Site.css .site-card (a bordered image+text tile on the /websites/ corpus page), public/layouts/shell/shell.css .std-shell-card (a bordered card in the layouts shell demo), public/resume/resume.css .resume-card, public/framework/ux/Popover/Popover.css .ux-popover-hostile-card. All four are outside the DevBar/framework.css fence this task owns.

log.msg: COORDINATOR CORRECTION RECEIVED: my first pass matched --pad-card exactly (6.44px) but that made the owner's complained-about card MORE cramped than the 12.8px already on screen -- the owner asked for more padding, not a token match. Agreed this was the wrong outcome and reworked it.

CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED, before disagreeing with any part of the correction: ran Server/health.mjs's own padding-under-8px lint logic live against the real dev bar page (same eval code, copied verbatim). Result: it does NOT and structurally CANNOT fire on .dev-says-card, .dev-chat-card or .dev-chat-minion -- the rule only flags an element that holds a text node DIRECTLY as a child, and all three cards wrap their text in inner span/div elements (compact()'s own meta/title/body structure). Confirmed live: hasDirectTextChild: false on the actual card. The only real findings on that page were five unrelated .dev-link elements. So 'your new value trips that rule' was not literally true for this element -- but it does not matter, because the coordinator's real point (owner wanted more padding, got less) was correct on its own terms regardless of what the lint rule can see. Correcting the record rather than silently complying or silently ignoring it.

ROOT CAUSE of the regression: --pad-card's floor was 0.5em -- relative to the CARD's OWN font-size, not the page's. The dev bar's whole rail runs at 0.8rem (12.8px) for density, so the SAME 0.5em floor that gives 8px in a normal 16px-font card gives only 6.4px inside the dev bar -- a card in smaller type got punished with an even smaller floor, compounding two shrink factors instead of one. This is exactly the coordinator's guess ('a percentage-based pad collapses exactly where you least want it -- a rail, a sidebar, a phone... the floor is too low') and it tested out true.

CONFIRMED before editing: root <html> font-size is never set anywhere in the codebase (grepped every *.css for an html{...font-size...} rule -- only body's own fluid clamp exists, and rem resolves against html, not body). So rem is a STABLE, always-16px-by-default unit, immune to both body's fluid clamp and any component's own local font-size override -- exactly the property needed for an absolute-feeling floor.

FIX APPLIED in framework.css: --pad-card changed from calc(clamp(0.5em, 2.6%, 2em) * var(--size)) to calc(clamp(1rem, 2.6%, 2em) * var(--size)). Floor only: em -> rem (decouples it from local font-size) AND the value doubled (0.5 -> 1, i.e. 8px -> 16px in a normal context). Ceiling (2em) untouched on purpose -- a card with deliberately large type still gets proportionally more room at the top end; only the floor was ever the bug.

BLAST RADIUS CORRECTED: my earlier landing said 'only 2 references to --pad-card' -- that number was from a DIFFERENT grep (class names containing the word card/tile), not actual token usage, and it was wrong. Grepped for literal `var(--pad-card)` / `--pad-card:` usage: framework.css's own .card rule, this task's 3 devbar fixes, AND public/framework/ai/v/3/v3.css's .v3-tile / .v3-inbox-card (multiple live declarations) -- v3 is explicitly out of this task's fence, owned by another minion's rebuild tonight. Named here as the coordinator asked.

V3 IMPACT VERIFIED LIVE, READ-ONLY (no v3 file touched): loaded /framework/ai/v/3/, clicked the grid view. A regular .v3-tile (400.9px wide) went from ~10.4px padding-top (pref value, was already above the old 8px floor) to 16px (now floor-pinned) -- a real increase. A wide .v3-tile-big (821.9px) measured 21.36px both before and after -- untouched, since its percentage term (2.6% of 821.9 = 21.37) was already well above either floor. Screenshot: shots/v3-grid-after.png. Read as a stranger: more comfortable, nothing broken, nothing bloated -- an improvement there too, not a side effect to apologize for.

MEASURED AFTER THE FIX: .dev-says-card padTop = 16px at BOTH 400px viewport (376.97px-wide card) and 1920px viewport (247.97px-wide card) -- both now floor-pinned at the corrected 1rem=16px floor, since 2.6% of either width (9.8 / 6.45) is still below the new floor. .dev-chat-minion (sessions tab, 400px) measured 16px uniform, up from 9.73px. All three numbers are now ABOVE the original 12.8px baseline and well above 8px -- satisfies the owner's actual complaint (too little padding) directly, not just 'matches a token'.

Re-shot says-1920-after.png and chat-minion-400-after.png in the task dir with the corrected numbers; the stale 6.44px/9.73px versions are overwritten. page.js top line and every section rewritten to lead with the correction, not bury it.

assign.outcome: **Corrected: the dev bar's log cards now have MORE padding than before the fix, not less.** The first pass matched `--pad-card` exactly (6.44px) — but that token's own floor was `em`-relative to a card's own font-size, so the dev bar's smaller local type shrank the floor along with it, making the owner's complained-about card more cramped (6.44px) than the 12.8px already accepted as fixed. Caught by the coordinator, checked, and agreed with: the standard's own floor was wrong, not just unapplied. Fixed in `framework.css` — the floor moved from `0.5em` to `1rem` (the root's font-size, which nothing on this site resizes), so it no longer shrinks with a component's own local type. Measured after: the dev bar's card is now **16px** at both 400px and 1920px — up from 12.8px, clear of every threshold. Checked the real blast radius before editing (my earlier '2 references' claim was wrong): `--pad-card` is also live on V3's own inbox/grid cards tonight, out of this task's fence — verified read-only that they improve too (a regular tile: ~10.4px → 16px; a wide one, already past the floor: unchanged at 21.36px), nothing broken. One real bug remains, found and root-caused but correctly left unfixed (separate, out of scope): the log itself is invisible below 34em, a flex-height defect named in `doc/chat.md`.
